newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power firms amid plant outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power firms amid plant outages.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West firmed Monday, due largely to unplanned as well as planned outages at regional power plants, trade sources said.
"A couple of coal plants are down and that took a chunk out of supply," said a California power trader.

As expected, one of the two 670-megawatt (MW) units at PacifiCorp's Centralia plant in Washington state was restarted Saturday after being shut Thursday to repair a tube leak. But Centralia's other unit was taken off-line Saturday afternoon for similar work and will not be back up until late Monday, the company said.

Meanwhile, a 700-MW unit at the Colstrip plant in Montana remains off line after being shut Thursday for unplanned maintenance. It is expected to be back up no later than early Tuesday, Montana Power Co said Monday.
In addition, traders said the planned refueling outage starting Saturday of the 1,221-MW Palo Verde nuclear unit 1 in Arizona also helped support spot prices.
"Even though it was scheduled, the Palo Verde outage seemed to catch some people by surprise," said another trader.
Next-day California-Oregon border (COB) prices were last assessed at $18.00-19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $17.00-18.00 on Friday.
Palo Verde next-day power was quoted $19.00-20.00 per MWh, up from $18.00-19.00.
COB for October was last quoted $15.55-15.80 per MWh, up from $15.50-15.60 on Friday. October Palo Verde was quoted $16.00-16.25, up from $15.80-16.00 on Friday.
"Loads are really light. I think these prices are a short-term reaction," said a trader.
